notes: All 13 native groups were rebuilt after the authorized simurgh rename, against the renamed compiler and rebuilt host runtime. The pre-rename 82 checks are retained under output/sdk-super-before-simurgh and are not reused as current acceptance. Ordinary verification reuses the complete post-rename run; compiler/test/verifier hashes remained unchanged during this native rebuild.

Public externally extendable SDK classes from linked libraries are allowed; original analyzer constructor/interface/base/final/sealed rules remain authoritative. SDK mixin applications remain rejected.

SDK ancestor AST signatures and public field accessors generate genuine super calls with instantiated type parameters, defaults, getters/setters/operators, and rewritten explicit type arguments. SDK implementation/storage are not copied into user code.

The baseline retains both SDK implementation and extension contracts, including LinkedListEntry (extendable but not externally implementable). A patch can first add SDK subclasses without rewriting SDK libraries.

Existing AOT consumers observe patched ListBase indexing through SDK sort and iterator/map methods. Defaults, first SDK super call, MutableRectangle field mutation, MapView index writes and AssertionError/Error field values and stack trace presence/identity match original-source AOT.

The SDK super index fixture retains distinct Object? read keys and int write keys. An invalid key fails before RHS evaluation; a valid key proceeds to the String value check. Compound/postfix/null-aware indexing also passed.

Original AOT holds a patch-only MapBase object through an SDK values view and a patch-only Error with a native inherited stack trace across GC. It reads 30 and preserves nonnull stack trace identity after collection.

Business mixin on-constraints traverse the business superclass SDK ancestry. Internal bridge signatures on implicit interfaces are satisfied only for generated members; original source members/noSuchMethod remain unchanged, and actual inheritance retains real bridge bodies.

The initial native mixin regression revealed missing generated-interface members. Its failure is retained; the concurrent incomplete ordinary run was intentionally stopped before compiler edits and is not counted as passing. Final full verification was restarted after the fix.

A full ordinary run exposed external pub regeneration of a deliberately incomplete temporary package configuration. Before/after snapshots captured the restored dependency. Test copies now omit only root pubspec/lock files for hand-written configurations while retaining dependency manifests; missing-package, relocation and language-change checks passed after isolation, followed by a full ordinary rerun.
Only these 13 current-compiler native groups were rebuilt, not the full historical native suite. Eager bridge/retention costs and mobile performance have not been measured.
remaining: SDK mixin applications and SDK mixin ancestry, direct super access to user-declared fields, and broader SDK/signature coverage
